12 August 2026 · Total solar eclipse at sunset · Mallorca

Watching from …

✓  …

All of Mallorca lies inside the 290 km-wide path of totality, so the question is the terrain: mid-eclipse comes at 20:31 CEST with the sun only 2.5° above the horizon at bearing 287° (WNW). This page ray-traces the SRTM elevation model from every stretch of coast — and in detail from all 13 viable viewpoints. Click a highlighted row in the ranked table to switch the map's bearing fan, the horizon panorama and the recommendations to that spot.

Timeline for the evening

Time (CEST)What happens
by 19:30Be in position — parked, walked in, standing spot and return path chosen. No shade on the coast or the summits: water, hat, eclipse glasses, headlamp.
19:35First contact — the Moon takes its first bite. Glasses on for every partial phase.
≈20:10Light turns thin and silvery; temperature starts dropping.
≈20:28Sharp shadows, Venus out, the umbra darkens the WNW sky.
20:31:05Totality begins — glasses off; corona, horizon colours all around.
20:32:41Totality ends (≈1 m 36 s) — glasses back on as the first flash returns.
20:44–20:50The still-eclipsed crescent reaches the horizon — per-site "visible until": Es Trenc beach 20:44, Cura 20:46, Cap Blanc 20:47, Presos cliff and Port de Valldemossa ≈20:48.
20:46True sea-level sunset. The sun goes down still partially eclipsed.

    Method & caveats

    Solar track computed for the south coast (NOAA solar geometry + standard refraction; sun position varies by under 0.03° across the island): totality at 20:31 CEST, sun at refracted altitude 2.5°, azimuth 287.4°; sea-level sunset 20:46 at azimuth 289.6°. Terrain: NASA SRTM 1-arc-second tiles; road network, viewpoints and place names from OpenStreetMap (© OSM contributors, ODbL). For each site, rays were marched at 60–90 m steps out to 110 km across azimuths 270–310°, with earth curvature and k = 0.13 refraction; horizon values are clamped at each site's elevation-dipped sea horizon. Per-spot datasets also ship as standalone JSON files under data/.

    Caveats: SRTM carries ±5–10 m vertical error and doesn't see buildings or trees — check your exact standing spot for pines and walls. Contact times vary by ±1 min across the island. The real enemy at 2.5° altitude is a distant haze or cloud band on the sea horizon; a Saharan dust episode (calima) would dim every site equally — check the aerosol forecast a day out.

    Sources: timeanddate — Palma circumstances · Absolute Eclipse — Mallorca guide · Visit Palma · Wikipedia — Solar eclipse of 12 Aug 2026
